land.text: Béjaïa, taken by Pedro Navarro in 1510 from Sultan Abdelaziz

predecessors.note: The Capture page: 'Sultan Abdelaziz, of a branch of the Hafsid dynasty, ruled the emirate'.

land.text: Béjaïa, surrendered by Alfonso de Peralta on 27 September 1555 to Salah Rais

successors.note: The Kuku page has Kuku put in charge of the immediate hinterland, including the wood supply for the city (no year).

capitals.name: Béjaïa (Bugía)
capitals.note: The Spanish held 'the imperial fort (Bordj Moussa), the sea fort (Bordj Abdelkader), and the Casbah'; the garrison was about 100 men in the presidio under Luis Peralta and then Alonso Peralta (Féraud: 500 to 1,000 men across three forts).

correction.text: Béjaïa, the walled city with a palisade from the Sidi Aïssa district to the sea, held by Spain

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page says the Spanish held three works (Bordj Moussa, Bordj Abdelkader and the Casbah) and no hinterland; the 1510 page describes 'a palisade from the Sidi Aïssa district to the sea' and a reduced wall perimeter. The 25 km circle is the smallest the grid can draw and overstates a city by a wide margin.

ledger.note: 1510: Pedro Navarro takes Béjaïa. He 'set sail from Spain on 1 January 1510 and reached Béjaïa on 5 January'; the Arab sources place the fall in late May ('fifth day of the month of safar in the year 915', 25 May 1510); an inscription on a Casbah door reads 1509; the 1555 page: the city 'was taken by the Spaniards in 1510', with another passage giving 1509.

27 September 1555: Alfonso de Peralta surrenders the Casbah. He 'surrendered on September 27, after 25 days of siege without food or ammunition'; on 28 September 'the Algerians indefinitely occupied the city'.

1555: Spanish rule ends. The 1510 page: the Spanish 'lost the city again 45 years later' to Salah Rais and the Kingdom of Kuku; Béjaïa 'passed under Ottoman rule' and Salah Rais took the plain and the Yemma Gouraya mountain.

wars.name: Barbarossa and Kuku siege of Béjaïa
wars.outcome: In 1512 Ahmed ou el Kadhi 'allied with the Barbarossa brothers, Aruj and Hayreddin, in an attempt to recapture Bejaia'; the Kuku page: 'Béjaïa siege, 1512: Aruj Barbarossa's siege failed, and he lost an arm.'
wars.note: The Barbarossas were not yet a state with a dossier, so only Kuku is a belligerent.

wars.name: Salah Rais's siege of Béjaïa
wars.outcome: Salah Rais besieged the Spanish for 25 days; Alfonso de Peralta surrendered on 27 September 1555; Salah Rais allied with the Sultan of Kuku against Abdelaziz el Abbes of the Kalaa.

certainty.note: One walled city; the pages give no extent and the 25 km circle is the grid's minimum.

notes: Cliopatria has no Bougie row (its Kingdom of Spain row starts in 1516 and the Hafsid row carries the Constantinois to 1555; see the Hafsid dossier notes). Dates: Pedro Navarro reached Béjaïa on 5 January 1510 and the city fell in late May 1510 on the Arab sources, while a Casbah door inscription reads 1509 (the Hafsid dossier has 1509); the Hafsids of Béjaïa infobox gives 9 November 1510. The Hafsid emir's flight: Emir Abderrahmane withdrew to the Kalaa of Beni Abbes and set up a principality (the kingdom-of-beni-abbas dossier), and Abdelaziz's brother Abu Bakr, prince of Constantine, killed him in battle at Takerkat (no year). The 1555 page's Spanish strength differs by source: about 100 men in the presidio, or 500 to 1,000 men across the three forts (Féraud), or 1,000 men and a few dozen horses (Braudel). Other Spanish enclaves taken in the same years (the Peñón of Algiers, Tripoli in 1510, Melilla, the Peñón de Vélez) are not on the pages opened here.
